new.title: Pose with the Trojan Horse from the film Troy
new.desc: The wooden horse on the Çanakkale waterfront is the prop built for the 2004 film Troy, given to the city afterwards. It stands on the Kordon, the seafront promenade, facing the Dardanelles.
new.tip: Come at sunset when the strait traffic lights up; it is free and open at all hours.
new.q: Truva Atı, Kordon, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Tour Çimenlik Castle and the Naval Museum
new.desc: Mehmed II built Çimenlik (Kale-i Sultaniye) in 1462-63 to lock the Dardanelles together with Kilitbahir opposite. Today it houses the Çanakkale Naval Museum, with a replica of the minelayer Nusret and relics of the 1915 naval battle.
new.tip: Allow about an hour; the park around the castle has cannon and 1915 artillery pieces.
new.q: Çimenlik Kalesi, Cevatpaşa, Çanakkale

new.title: Find the 1897 Çanakkale Clock Tower
new.desc: The five-storey, 20 m clock tower was built in the late 1890s under the district governor Cemil Pasha. It marks the old square where the fish market and Yalı Caddesi meet.
new.tip: It sits on the way between the Kordon and the Naval Museum, so combine them in one walk.
new.q: Saat Kulesi, Yalı Caddesi, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: See Anatolian pottery at the Çanakkale Ceramics Museum
new.desc: Opened in 1997 as Türkiye's first ceramics museum, it is set in a restored Ottoman building and shows Hittite, Lydian, Roman and Ottoman pieces alongside Çanakkale's own pottery tradition. Visitors can also try making a pot.
new.tip: Ask at the desk about the hands-on pottery workshop.
new.q: Çanakkale Seramik Müzesi, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat warm peynir helvası at Kadir Usta
new.desc: Peynir helvası is the cheese-and-flour sweet of Çanakkale, cooked from fresh unsalted cheese and served hot, often with a scoop of ice cream. Kadir Usta is one of the best-known specialists in the city centre and usually has a queue.
new.tip: Order it hot (sıcak); it is rich, so share a portion.
new.q: Çanakkale Helvacısı Kadir Usta, Arap İbrahim Paşa Caddesi 24, Namık Kemal, Çanakkale

new.title: Try a sardine sandwich at Sardalye
new.desc: Sardalye, in a side street of the old centre, is known for its sardine sandwich, a nod to the sardine tradition of the strait. Locals use it for a quick, well-reviewed lunch.
new.tip: Go outside peak lunch hour; it is a small, fast place.
new.q: Sardalye, Küçük Hamam Sokak, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Order meze and fish at Yalova Restoran
new.desc: A long-running fish restaurant on Gümrük Sokak near the port, said to date back to 1940, serving meze and the day's catch. It is a classic for a sit-down fish dinner in town.
new.tip: Ask for the fish by weight and check the price first, as reviewers warn.
new.q: Yalova Restoran, Gümrük Sokak, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Browse the Aynalı Çarşı bazaar
new.desc: The covered Aynalı Çarşı is the old shopping street of the city, with small shops for local cheeses, olive products, ceramics and souvenirs. It connects the Kordon with the clock tower area.
new.tip: Buy Ezine cheese and Gelibolu halva here as gifts.
new.q: Aynalı Çarşı, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Ride the Çanakkale–Eceabat ferry across the Dardanelles
new.desc: The car-and-passenger ferries cross the narrowest part of the strait in about 30 minutes, past Çimenlik and Kilitbahir, where the 1915 naval battle took place. It is the classic way to reach the Gallipoli peninsula.
new.tip: Sit on the open top deck and buy a cheap simit on board.
new.q: Çanakkale Eceabat feribot iskelesi, Cevatpaşa, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Climb Kilitbahir Castle, the lock of the sea
new.desc: Fatih Sultan Mehmed built the clover-shaped castle in 1463 to close the Dardanelles with Çimenlik opposite. Its thick-walled central tower can be climbed for views down the strait.
new.tip: Take the short car ferry from Çanakkale; allow an hour for the tower and the Namazgah bastion nearby.
new.q: Kilitbahir Kalesi, Kilitbahir, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Walk the ruins of Troy at Hisarlık
new.desc: Troy, a UNESCO site, has nine main layers of settlement spanning about 4,000 years and is tied to Homer's Iliad. Schliemann dug here from 1871, and the site includes walls, a ramp and a wooden horse replica at the entrance.
new.tip: Go early or late in summer; combine with the Troy Museum next door and keep two hours for both.
new.q: Truva Antik Kenti, Tevfikiye, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Visit the award-winning Troy Museum
new.desc: Opened in October 2018 about 800 m from the ruins, the museum shows around 2,000 of its 40,000-plus finds, arranged from the Bronze Age to the Byzantine era.
new.tip: Visit the museum before the ruins so the finds make sense on site; a combined ticket exists.
new.q: Troya Müzesi, Tevfikiye, Merkez, Çanakkale

new.title: Explore the Roman baths of Alexandria Troas
new.desc: Founded around 310 BC and renamed Alexandria Troas in 301 BC, it became a major Roman port; the Apostle Paul sailed for Europe from here. Remains include the Herodes Atticus baths, the city walls and a harbour.
new.tip: Bring water and sun protection; there is little shade or signage.
new.q: Alexandria Troas Antik Kenti, Dalyan, Ezine, Çanakkale

new.title: See the temple of Apollo Smintheus at Gülpınar
new.desc: The Hellenistic sanctuary of Apollo Smintheus, the mouse god, is mentioned in the Iliad; its ruins stand near the village of Gülpınar and include Ionic column fragments and a relief frieze.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to Babakale; a small display stands beside the temple.
new.q: Smintheion Apollon Tapınağı, Gülpınar, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Visit Babakale Castle at Turkey's westernmost point
new.desc: The last Ottoman castle built in Anatolia, completed in the 1720s under Ahmed III to guard the cape against pirates. It overlooks the fishing harbour at Cape Baba, the westernmost point of mainland Turkey.
new.tip: Have tea in the harbour in the evening and check whether the castle is open that day.
new.q: Babakale Kalesi, Babakale, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Stand in the Doric Temple of Athena at Assos
new.desc: The 530 BC temple on the Assos acropolis is the only Doric temple in Asia Minor dedicated to Athena; six of its original 38 columns survive. Aristotle lived in Assos in the 340s BC and views reach Lesbos.
new.tip: Go in the evening for sunset and cooler air; the Hüdavendigar Mosque is just below.
new.q: Athena Tapınağı, Behramkale, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Taste honey-almond ice cream at Yahya Usta
new.desc: Yahya Usta is the best-known ice cream shop of Assos, famed for a honey-almond flavour. Several guides name it as the sweet stop after the Athena temple.
new.tip: Try the bal-badem (honey-almond) flavour.
new.q: Meşhur Assos Dondurması Yahya Usta, Behram, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat fish by the water at Assos harbour
new.desc: The small stone harbour below Behramkale has fish restaurants on the quay; Uzun Ev is named in local guides as a place to watch the sunset over a fish dinner. Look for kabak çiçeği dolması as a meze.
new.tip: Book a table by the water for sunset in summer.
new.q: Uzun Ev Restaurant, İskele Mevkii, Behram Yolu 30, Behram, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Learn olive oil history at the Adatepe museum
new.desc: Opened in 2001 in a former soap factory on the İzmir road, it was Türkiye's first olive-oil museum and shows presses, storage jars and harvest tools.
new.tip: Taste and buy the oil in the shop; check opening on the day.
new.q: Adatepe Zeytinyağı Müzesi, Küçükkuyu, Ayvacık, Çanakkale

new.title: Buy genuine Ezine cheese at Kudret Kahraman Peynircilik
new.desc: Ezine cheese, a protected white cheese from cow, sheep and goat milk, takes its name from this small town. Kudret Kahraman is a family dairy producing and selling in Ezine since 1993.
new.tip: Look for the geographical-indication label rather than 'Ezine-style' cheese.
new.q: Kudret Kahraman Peynircilik, Ezine, Çanakkale

new.title: Stand on Anzac Cove, where the Gallipoli landing began
new.desc: On 25 April 1915 Australian and New Zealand troops came ashore at this narrow 600 m beach, which became their base for eight months. Ari Burnu Cemetery and the Sphinx rock stand beside it.
new.tip: Come in the morning or off-peak; allow time for North Beach and Ari Burnu Cemetery.
new.q: Anzac Koyu, Arıburnu, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Pay respects at Lone Pine Cemetery
new.desc: Lone Pine, the Turkish Kanlısırt, was the scene of a ferocious Australian assault on 6-9 August 1915. The cemetery is the main memorial to Australians with no known grave; a Turkish inscription tells the battle from the other side.
new.tip: Combine with the nearby Turkish 57th Regiment memorial.
new.q: Lone Pine Şehitliği, Kanlısırt, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Climb to Conkbayırı, the hill of Atatürk
new.desc: Conkbayırı (Chunuk Bair) was taken by the Allies on 8 August 1915 and retaken by Mustafa Kemal's counter-attack. A New Zealand memorial and cemetery stand beside the Turkish monument.
new.tip: The one-way road from Kabatepe follows the old front line, so drive it slowly.
new.q: Conkbayırı Atatürk Anıtı ve Yeni Zelanda Anıtı, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Visit the 57th Regiment Memorial at Gallipoli
new.desc: Built in 1992, the memorial honours the 57th Infantry Regiment, which held the line at Arıburnu and whose men were told by Mustafa Kemal 'I do not order you to attack, I order you to die'. It has a fountain, prayer area and cemetery.
new.tip: Come in the quiet hours to appreciate the atmosphere.
new.q: 57. Alay Şehitliği, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Start at the Kabatepe War Museum
new.desc: The museum near Kabatepe displays weapons, uniforms and personal items recovered from the battlefields. It is the traditional first stop for the peninsula.
new.tip: Visit before touring the battlefields for context.
new.q: Çanakkale Destanı Tanıtım Merkezi, Kabatepe, Kemalpaşa, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Explore the 1659 Seddülbahir fortress at Cape Helles
new.desc: Built in 1659 under Turhan Sultan, Seddülbahir held the southern tip of the peninsula. It was damaged in the 1915 landings and later restored; the Helles Memorial is nearby.
new.tip: Visit the village and the cemeteries on the same drive.
new.q: Seddülbahir Kalesi, Seddülbahir, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: See the Çanakkale Martyrs' Memorial at Hisarlık
new.desc: The memorial on Hisarlık Hill, finished in 1960, honours the Turkish dead of the Gallipoli campaign. Four pillars support a concrete canopy; it is the most visited point in the Gallipoli Historical Site.
new.tip: Park once and walk around the memorial and its cemetery.
new.q: Çanakkale Şehitler Abidesi, Morto Koyu, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Order fish at Liman Balık in Eceabat
new.desc: A long-time favourite on İstiklal Caddesi with big windows over the small waterfront park, serving fresh fish and meze after a Gallipoli day.
new.tip: Sit by the window and try the grilled sea bream or the sardines.
new.q: Liman Balık Restaurant, İstiklal Caddesi 67, İsmetpaşa, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat Eceabat köfte at Gözde Köfteci
new.desc: Gözde Köfteci is a highly rated grill house in town known for its grilled meatballs, a local style of köfte.
new.tip: Order with piyaz and grilled peppers.
new.q: Gözde Köfte Çorba Salonu, Zübeyde Hanım Meydanı 38, Eceabat, Çanakkale

new.title: Taste GI-protected Gelibolu peynir helvası at Zafer
new.desc: Gelibolu cheese halva, said to go back about 700 years, is made only from fresh unsalted cheese, a little flour and sugar, and has a geographical indication. Zafer Tarihi Peynir Helvacısı serves it in the old centre.
new.tip: Eat it warm, plain or baked.
new.q: Tarihi Zafer Peynir Helvacısı, Yazıcızade, Atatürk Caddesi 33, Gelibolu, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat grilled sardines at Gelibolu Sardalya
new.desc: Gelibolu is the sardine town of the strait; the fish is grilled in vine leaves or salted in a recipe the town's Greek community left behind. Gelibolu Sardalya, near the quay, is praised for sardines and whiting.
new.tip: Order the grilled sardines in vine leaves in season.
new.q: Gelibolu Sardalya, İskele Meydanı, Gelibolu, Çanakkale

new.title: See Piri Reis' maps in the Gelibolu castle tower
new.desc: The small museum is housed in a stone tower of the Gelibolu fortress, a remnant of a Byzantine castle expanded by the Ottomans. It shows reproductions of Piri Reis' world maps, as the admiral was based in Gelibolu.
new.tip: Check opening hours; a Müzekart usually covers entry.
new.q: Piri Reis Müzesi, Gelibolu Kalesi, Gelibolu, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat soft Biga köftesi at Köfteci Akif
new.desc: Biga köfte is made only with beef, bread, onion and salt, and Köfteci Akif is a roughly 50-year-old shop locals recommend, serving it with piyaz. Kaymaklı peynir tatlısı is the sweet to follow.
new.tip: Order with piyaz and finish with the cheese dessert.
new.q: Köfteci Akif, Biga, Çanakkale

new.title: See the theatre and odeon of ancient Parion
new.desc: Parion was an Ionian colony on the Marmara coast near Biga, famous for its coins and a Roman odeon. Excavations have revealed the theatre, agora and a stretch of the city's sea wall.
new.tip: Visit in spring; bring sun protection.
new.q: Parion Antik Kenti, Kemer, Biga, Çanakkale

new.title: Walk the walls of Bozcaada Castle
new.desc: Mehmed II rebuilt the castle after the 1455 conquest; it has a bailey and a citadel with a moat to the south and is one of Türkiye's best-preserved island fortresses.
new.tip: Go for sunset views over the harbour and the vineyards.
new.q: Bozcaada Kalesi, Cumhuriyet, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Swim at Ayazma Beach on Bozcaada
new.desc: Ayazma is the island's best-known sandy cove on the south coast, near the Ayazma monastery and with a few restaurants and water-sports operators.
new.tip: Visit in the morning before the wind rises.
new.q: Ayazma Plajı, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Have coffee and patlıcanlı börek at Çınaraltı
new.desc: A plane-tree café on Çınar Çarşı Caddesi near the ferry quay, known for Turkish coffee, tea and patlıcanlı börek (aubergine pastry), and a good first stop on the island.
new.tip: Sit under the plane tree and order the patlıcanlı börek.
new.q: Çınaraltı Cafe, Çınar Çarşı Caddesi, Alaybey, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat calamari and meze at Vahit'in Yeri
new.desc: A classic meyhane near Ayazma Beach known for calamari and a spread of meze such as Girit ezme and börülce salad.
new.tip: Order the calamari and share a few meze.
new.q: Vahit'in Yeri, Ayazma Mevkii, Cumhuriyet, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Buy mastic-almond cookies at Çiçek Pastanesi
new.desc: A bakery in the old Greek quarter famous for its almond cookies flavoured with damla sakızı (mastic) as well as breads and cakes.
new.tip: Buy a box to take home.
new.q: Çiçek Pastanesi, Atatürk Caddesi, Rum Mahallesi, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Taste Bozcaada wines at Talay Şarap Evi
new.desc: Bozcaada's volcanic soil and wind produce distinctive local grapes; Talay Şarap Evi is a long-established wine house where visitors can taste several wines for a fee and buy bottles.
new.tip: Ask for a tasting of the local Kuntra and Karasakız.
new.q: Talay Şarap Evi, Cumhuriyet, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: See Polente Lighthouse at the island's western tip
new.desc: Polente is the lighthouse on the western end of Bozcaada, a spot for sunset with the island's wind turbines nearby. It lies at the windswept end of the island road.
new.tip: Go at sunset and bring a layer; the wind is strong.
new.q: Polente Feneri, Bozcaada, Çanakkale

new.title: Have the village breakfast at Çınaraltı in Tepeköy
new.desc: Tepeköy (Agridia) is the old Greek hill village, and Çınaraltı under the plane tree is known for sigara böreği, menemen and organic jams on its breakfast spread.
new.tip: Come for a late breakfast, and try the daily home-style dishes.
new.q: Çınaraltı, Tepeköy, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: Eat kid and island dishes at Barba Yorgo
new.desc: A village taverna in Tepeköy run in the Greek-island style, known for goat kid (oğlak) and fish.
new.tip: Book ahead in summer.
new.q: Barba Yorgo, Tepeköy, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: Visit Kaleköy and its harbour castle at sunset
new.desc: Kaleköy (Kastro) on the north-east coast has a medieval castle above a small port of stone houses and a plane-tree square. It is the island's favourite sunset spot.
new.tip: Have dinner at the harbour and stay for sunset.
new.q: Kaleköy, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: Windsurf or swim at Aydıncık Beach
new.desc: Aydıncık (Kefalos) is the island's best-known beach, over a kilometre of golden sand on the south coast with a windsurf school operating since 2004.
new.tip: Mornings are calm; the wind rises by midday.
new.q: Aydıncık Plajı, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: Swim at Gizli Liman beach in Uğurlu
new.desc: Uğurlu on the western coast is known for its golden beach and calm hidden harbour, with a Neolithic mound nearby that goes back about 7,000 years. It is also the island's sunset coast.
new.tip: Watch the sun go down from the harbour.
new.q: Gizli Liman, Uğurlu, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: Hike to Marmaros Waterfall
new.desc: Marmaros waterfall is a lesser-known natural attraction on the north coast, reached on foot through the island's interior; a pebble beach lies about an hour's walk away.
new.tip: Go in spring when the water flows.
new.q: Marmaros Şelalesi, Gökçeada, Çanakkale

new.title: See the old Greek houses of Zeytinli
new.desc: Zeytinli (Agios Theodoros) is a preserved Rum village among olive groves; its stone houses, church and washing-houses are protected, and Patriarch Bartholomew I was born here.
new.tip: Stop for coffee in the village square.
new.q: Zeytinliköy, Gökçeada, Çanakkale
